title: Define burst-tolerant SLO lanes and canary burn-rate framework for hosted inference
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Hosted customers experience short high-traffic bursts (traffic spikes, enterprise cron jobs, or batch inference windows) that cause p99 latency and error rates to degrade temporarily. Current single-band SLOs either force overly conservative throttling (hurting throughput/cost) or allow outage-blind rollouts. We need an SLO and rollout gating framework that explicitly models burst tolerance, separates steady-state and burst lanes, and ties canary gating to a burn-rate computation that factors latency, error, and quality regressions.

Goal: Define lane-specific SLO targets (Steady, Burst, Economical), acceptance criteria and canary-stage burn-rate thresholds; produce rollout gate definitions and automated rollback triggers for hosted model deploys. Deliverables: SLO table with formulas, canary sequencing for traffic ramp, monitoring queries and alert thresholds, test harness requirements and PRD acceptance criteria.

Scope: Hosted API (text generation + chat). Does not include Dedicated or Private (follow-on follow-ups will adapt lanes to committed capacity).
background_and_rationale: Existing latency SLOs are single-band p99 <= 300ms and availability 99.9% which mask transient tail spikes that occur during bursts.
Customers want predictable behavior during predictable bursts (e.g., product launches) and not be penalized by inflexible enforcement that reduces throughput unnecessarily.

Canary gate decisions today rely on aggregated p95/p99 snapshots; we need time-aware burn-rate logic that evaluates risk over the canary hold window and is sensitive to tail regressions and quality drift.
slo_definitions: Steady lane (default production): p50 <= 40ms, p90 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms, availability >= 99.95%, error rate <= 0.5% over 1h windows
Burst lane (short-duration high concurrency): p50 <= 60ms, p90 <= 180ms, p99 <= 600ms, availability >= 99.5%, error rate <= 1% measured over 15m rolling windows
Economical lane (low-cost/queued best-effort): p50 <= 120ms, p90 <= 400ms, p99 <= 1s, availability >= 99.0%, error rate <= 2%

Quality floor: model-output quality metric (semantic-similarity score against golden-sets or rerank lift) must not regress by >2% absolute during canary windows or a separate quality SLO breach is triggered.
slo_formula_and_burn_rate: Define error budget = 1 - availability_target. Compute burn rate as (observed_bad_fraction / allowed_bad_fraction) normalized to the canary window length.
Bad fraction combines: latency_breach_fraction (requests > p99 threshold), error_fraction (5xx or model failure), and quality_breach_fraction (golden-set failures weighted heavier).

Example: For Steady lane: availability 99.95% -> allowed_bad_fraction = 0.0005. If over 1h canary we observe combined_bad_fraction = 0.0015, burn_rate = 0.0015 / 0.0005 = 3.0 meaning we are burning 3x the budget and must pause/rollback according to gates.
canary_sequence_and_gates: Stage 0 - Smoke: 0.5% traffic for 10 minutes. Automatic fail if any 5xx spike >0.2% absolute or quality regression >2%.

Stage 1 - Small canary: 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Gate evaluates cumulative burn_rate <= 2.0 and p99_delta <= +20% relative to baseline. Hold if burn_rate between 1.0 and 2.0 pending manual review. Automatic rollback if burn_rate > 2.0 or quality breach detected.
Stage 2 - Ramp: 25% traffic for 45 minutes. Gate requires burn_rate <= 1.0 and no sustained p99 increases beyond configured envelope; otherwise revert to previous variant and mark as Failed Canary.
Stage 3 - Full roll: 100% gradual shift remaining over 60 minutes if all prior gates pass; final verification window of 24h with alerting on slow burn-rate changes.
automated_rollback_triggers: Absolute threshold: >1% 5xx across canary window -> immediate rollback.
Burn-rate threshold: burn_rate >= 2.0 in any canary stage -> immediate rollback.
Quality threshold: semantic-similarity drop >2% absolute on golden-set over the canary window -> immediate rollback.
Tail-latency shock: sustained p99 increase >2x baseline during the stage -> immediate rollback.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard card: lane-specific p50/p90/p99 heatmap, burn-rate timeseries, quality drift timeseries, error-rate histogram by tenant.
Alert: Canary burn-rate >1.5 for 15m -> pager to oncall + notify PM and release owner.
Alert: Quality drift on golden-set >1% -> notify ML evaluation team and pause rollout (non-urgent page).
Contract test: per-canary-run synthetic traffic generator that mimics 3 traffic patterns: baseline, burst spike (5x QPS for 2 minutes), and mixed complexity (long sequences).
acceptance_criteria: SLO table implemented in central SLO registry and surfaced in Console with lane labels and computed burn-rate per canary run.
Runbook & automation: canary pipeline implements the 4 stages with programmable gates and automated rollback triggers as defined.
Test harness: synthetic canary job able to reproduce burst spike and assert that lanes behave within thresholds in 90% of simulator runs.
Observability: dashboard and alerts described above present and validated by SRE during staging deployments.
Contract tests: end-to-end smoke and burst tests pass in CI for the runtime-1.19 release branch before GA promotion.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: Weighting of quality vs availability in burn-rate: proposed to weight quality breaches 2x errors; need ML team sign-off on multiplier.
Burst lane economic cost: Broader burst tolerance increases infra cost; product must decide acceptable tradeoff for hosted multi-tenant pools.
Tenant-level exemptions: Some big tenants may require bespoke SLOs; need policy for per-tenant rollback vs global rollback semantics.
decisions_made: Adopt lane-based SLOs (Steady/Burst/Economical) and compute combined burn-rate using weighted sum of latency, error, and quality breaches.
Automated rollback thresholds finalized: burn_rate >= 2.0 immediate rollback; 1.0-2.0 hold for manual review during small canary stage.
Quality metric: use semantic-similarity AUC measured against curated golden-sets for canaries; regression >2% triggers rollback.
implementation_notes: SRE to extend current canary pipeline (github.com/redwood/canary-pipeline) with burn-rate evaluator module (inputs: lane config, baseline metrics, golden-set scorer).
Metrics: implement new Prometheus metric redwood_slo_breach_fraction{lane,stage} and burn_rate gauge. Console to read burn_rate via telemetry API.
CI: add synthetic burst scenario to pre-release test matrix and require green for merge to runtime-1.19 branch.
